column7: The New Covenant is a transformative relationship between God and His people, established through the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Unlike the Old Covenant, which was focused on external laws, the New Covenant emphasizes internal transformation and grace. It was inaugurated by Jesus at the Last Supper, where He declared that His blood would establish this covenant, replacing the repeated animal sacrifices of the Old Covenant with His once-for-all atonement (Luke 22:20; Hebrews 9:12; Hebrews 10:10). Through this sacrifice, the New Covenant provides complete forgiveness and cleansing from sin, fulfilling the requirement for a perfect and permanent reconciliation with God (Jeremiah 31:34; Hebrews 8:12; Hebrews 10:12-18).
